raw_response:
Answer: A
Reason: The chest X-rays demonstrate a massive right-sided pneumothorax with significant mediastinal shift to the right and an abnormal cardiac silhouette, which are classic radiographic signs of right-sided cardiac herniation into the pleural cavity following intrapericardial pneumonectomy. This mechanical displacement causes acute haemodynamic compromise by kinking the great vessels and impairing venous return.
